SONA Exercise & Eating Study - Study Procedures and Measures EMBARK Lab 2026-10-29 Study Overview The SONA Exercise & Eating Study (Exercise Motivations and Eating Behaviors; UT Austin investigator: Katherine Schaumberg, PhD) is an online survey study of exercise and eating motivations and behaviors, run through the UT Austin SONA research participation system. Participants complete a single REDCap survey session (about 1.5–2 hours) and receive 2 SONA course credits for completing the survey in full. The survey covers demographics, medical and treatment history, alcohol and drug use, height and weight; exercise habits and motivations; thoughts and feelings related to exercise, body image, weight gain, self-esteem, mood, mental health, and self-worth; how exercise may affect relationships with others; and hypothetical scenarios asking whether participants would keep exercising under different conditions (e.g., when sick or injured). No directly identifiable information (e.g., name, date of birth) is collected. This codebook documents every variable in the study’s REDCap project (PID 796), organized by measure. It follows the structure of the EMBARK Lab Meta Codebook so SONA measures can be compared with the lab’s other projects. All Measures — every variable, organized by measure, with descriptions, value coding, and scoring. Data Requests and Terms of Use — how to request SONA data. ED100K.V3 (Thornton et al., 2018), a self-report eating disorder assessment based on the SCID-5. It assesses current and lifetime eating disorder symptoms and includes items from the Dieting and Weight History Questionnaire (variables beginning wdqhq_), lab ED-history items (edhistory_, dcf_), EDE-Q items (edeq_), and EDDS items (edds_). It covers weight history (current, highest, lowest, set-point weight and BMI), menstrual history, binge eating, compensatory behaviors, driven exercise, restriction, and weight/shape concern. This measure is not yet validated. Scoring Weights entered in kilograms are converted to pounds (*_correct_plus), BMIs and weight-suppression values are computed, and diagnostic variables follow DSM-5 algorithms for threshold and sub-clinical (past and current) Anorexia Nervosa, Atypical Anorexia Nervosa, Bulimia Nervosa, Binge Eating Disorder, and Purging Disorder. Diagnostic variables are coded 0 = criteria not met, 1 = criteria met. Chapter 4 Data Requests and Terms of Use

Chapter 4 Data Requests and Terms of Use We aim to share data from the SONA Exercise & Eating Study with all interested parties. Depending on the data necessary for analysis, this may include providing collaborative access to the data and completing a data transfer and use agreement. We expect most data requests will take 2-4 weeks for administrative processing. In order to request data use, please complete the following steps: 1. Send an email with the title ‘SONA data use’ to embarklab@austin.utexas.edu with the following information: a. Name, affiliation, training status and year (e.g. second-year graduate student; post-baccalaureate research coordinator, first-year postdoc, assistant professor) b. Tentative title for proposed analysis and 1-paragraph description c. Two identified EMBARK Lab collaborators you would be interested in working with 2. Book a 15-minute meeting with Dr. Schaumberg to discuss your idea. For secondary analysis projects that exclusively use SONA data, Dr. Schaumberg will serve as senior (last) author, and at least one additional EMBARK Lab collaborator will join as an author on the project. Alternative arrangements can be discussed if SONA is one of multiple data sources for a project.
